description: The agent must write a valid Octave/MATLAB script that chains together several non-trivial idioms from the SKILL.md: (1) It must parse the CSV and represent missing fields as NaN — critically, it must use isnan() to detect NaN values, never '== NaN' (which is always false per the SKILL.md). (2) When applying the calibration gain × raw_value, it must use the element-wise operator '.*' rather than '*', since '*' would perform matrix multiplication and could give wrong results or errors. (3) When computing mean/max/min, it must either use the 'omitnan' flag (e.g., mean(x, 'omitnan')) or manually filter via isnan(), so NaN entries are excluded from statistics. (4) It must NOT use 'i' or 'j' as loop variable names, as these shadow the imaginary unit in MATLAB/Octave — a classic trap documented in the SKILL.md. (5) The final JSON must contain correct numeric statistics for all four channels. The key discriminative traps are: using isnan() instead of == NaN, using .* instead of *, using 'omitnan' or equivalent, and avoiding i/j as loop counters.
